description: File-level backup of named paths INSIDE a guest (ADR-012 §3.1) — the subset capability, as opposed to backup:vm's whole-guest snapshot.
_note: install/update-service.sh provision the PBS side (namespace fs/<module>, a write-no-delete login scoped to it, the client-side encryption key) and deploy the guest-side runner + timer. That is a reconcile with domain knowledge (lib/pbs-fs.sh), not a per-field set, so every field is apply:'reconcile'. The capture schedule is the same Site -> Environment -> Module cascade backup:vm uses (backup.schedule, §3.2).

backup.description: The module-level backup policy object. Under backup:filesystem only `filesystemPaths` is service-specific; `enabled`, `retention`, `exclude` and `schedule` are the shared cascade fields also read by backup:vm.

filesystemPaths.description: Absolute paths inside the guest to capture (ADR-012 §2.7/§3.1). Each becomes one PBS archive in the module's fs/<module> namespace. Only meaningful for a module declaring backup:filesystem, and only supported on guest OS types TAPPaaS knows the layout of (NixOS today) — the service install fails loudly on any other, rather than capturing something half-right. A declared path that does not exist in the guest fails the capture: a backup that silently stopped covering something is the failure this ADR exists to prevent.

backup.note: Authored on the consuming module, alongside the dependsOn/integratesWith backup:filesystem relationship that opts it in.
backup.changeNote: Which paths inside the guest are captured. Changing it changes future captures only; nothing already stored is touched, and the guest is not disturbed.
